records.subject: Demand for establishment of a permanent Bench of Gauhati High Court in Silchar, Assam.
records.SM_Text:
Ms. Sushmita Dev:

I seek to raise the need to strengthen access to justice for the people of the Barak Valley in Assam through the establishment of a permanent Bench of the Gauhati High Court at Silchar. Access to justice cannot depend upon geography or the financial capacity of a litigant. Yet, thousands of citizens from the districts of Cachar, Hailakandi and Karimganj have to travel to nearly 343 kilometres to Guwahati to approach the High Court. The cost of travel, accommodation, loss of wages and repeated court visits places an undue burden on farmers, daily-wage workers, women, senior citizens and small traders, thereby often discouraging them from pursuing legitimate legal remedies. The Barak Valley is home to more than 36 lakh people, but despite its sizeable population and distinct geographical location, it continues to remain without a permanent Bench of the Gauhati High Court. This gap undermines the constitutional promise of equal access to justice and warrants urgent attention. Access to justice is an integral facet of the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution.

          I, therefore, urge the Government to initiate the necessary consultations with the authorities concerned for the early establishment of a permanent Bench at Silchar. I also urge the Government to evolve objective criteria for establishing additional High Court Benches in underserved regions.

(ENDS)

records.subject: DEMAND FOR RELEASE OF BIOMETRIC DATA COLLECTED UNDER N.R.C. AND REMOVAL OF ANOMALY
records.SM_Text:
MS. SUSHMITA DEV (WEST BENGAL): Sir, updation of National Register of Citizens (NRC) was conducted in Assam under the supervision of the Supreme Court (SC). A draft NRC was published on 30.07.18 leaving out 40,70,707 persons as ineligible for inclusion. Vide order dated 13.08.19, the SC directed the NRC coordinator to set up a security regime for NRC biometric data as per Aadhaar regime. On 31.08.2019, a final list of NRC was released. Twenty-one lakh people were included and about 19 lakh were left out.

The biometrics have been withheld of about 26 lakh people including those whose names appeared in the NRC final draft list citing the Modalities. Clause 9 of the said Modalities states that once the final NRC has been published, persons who are included in it will be given an Aadhaar number as citizens. However, that has not happened on the grounds that the process of claims and objections have to be completed which can take a long time. As a consequence, lakhs of people are deprived of basic amenities connected to Aadhaar, even though they are not declared as foreigners depriving them of their Fundamental Right of life, livelihood, education and prevents access to Government schemes, requiring mandatory Aadhaar registration. The court has stated that no coercive action shall be taken against the people left out of the NRC until final notification.

The Central Government should take steps either in court or other legislative action to release the biometric data and remove this anomaly.

(Ends)
